name: Crawlee
summary: Crawlee is a free, open source library you run on your own server to crawl and scrape sites with plain HTTP requests or a real headless browser.

free_plan_covers.note: Free and open source with no usage cap; you can run as many crawls as your own server can handle.

first_paid_usd_month.note: No paid plan; it's a free library, so your only real costs are your own server (or serverless compute) and any proxies you choose to use.

portability.note: It's plain Node.js code (Playwright, Puppeteer, or Cheerio underneath) that runs on any server, container, or job runner you choose.

scraper_runs.note: Crawlee is a library you install and run inside your own server code or background job, not a hosted service.

js_rendering.note: PlaywrightCrawler and PuppeteerCrawler drive a real browser for JavaScript-heavy pages at no extra cost beyond installing Playwright or Puppeteer alongside Crawlee.

ai_ready_output.note: Crawlee hands you parsed HTML through Cheerio or a live browser page; turning that into clean Markdown or structured data for an AI model is code you write yourself.

price_per_1k_pages.value: Free software, so there's no per-page charge. You pay only for the server (or serverless compute) it runs on and for any proxies you choose to use.
price_per_1k_pages.note: Matches its open source, self-hosted model; cost depends entirely on your own hosting and proxy choices, not on Crawlee itself.

setup.step: No account needed; install it into your project with npm install crawlee playwright.
Create a PlaywrightCrawler with a requestHandler that reads the page (for example page.title()) and saves it with Dataset.pushData().
Call crawler.run([...startUrls]) from a server script or background job; results land in ./storage/datasets by default, so forward or copy them to durable storage before the job ends.

builder_notes: Run crawls from a background job or server script, not from a request a user is waiting on; a crawl can take much longer than a normal page load.
Crawlee's default dataset storage is local files, which don't survive most serverless or container redeploys, so save results somewhere durable if you need to keep them.
Respect each target site's robots.txt and terms of service; Crawlee will crawl whatever you point it at, it doesn't check for you.
